suggestion: State offline-start as NEW work and specify it: adopt the client-generated run id as authoritative, add a `create_run` WAL op, make `Run.__init__` non-fatal on an unreachable target, and define what `run.url`/`run_id` mean before the server has ever seen the run. Or drop the "same machinery, no special mode" claim.

section: §3 ("Ingest today = three modes") and §6 ("Kept and promoted")
claim: §3 states `drain_wal()` replay is "exposed as `cairn sync`", and §6 builds the whole durability story on "`cairn sync` replays after process death". `cairn sync` cannot replay the client WAL today, and no code anywhere discovers orphaned client WAL files.
evidence: `sync_cmd` builds its transport via `_client()` = `Transport(_config.resolve_server())` with no `wal=` argument (cairn/cli.py:443-444, 691-702), so `Transport._wal is None` (transport.py:74) and `drain_wal()` returns 0 immediately (`if not self._wal or not self._wal.has_pending: return 0`, transport.py:302-305). Worse, `sync_cmd` early-returns "no spill to sync" when `default_spill_dir()` is missing (cli.py:695-698) — that is `user_cache_dir("cairn")/pending` (transport.py:30-31), a *different* directory from the WAL's `user_cache_dir("cairn")/wal` (wal.py:36-37). The only WAL-scanning code in the tree is `cairn/server/wal_ingest.py:311-316`, which scans the repo-dir `.cairn/wals/` — i.e. exactly the `local_wal` mode §6 retires. Nothing reads `default_wal_dir()` except `WriteAheadLog` itself.
suggestion: Reclassify cross-process WAL recovery as new work in §6/S2: a WAL-dir scanner that enumerates `{run_id}.wal.jsonl`, reconstructs a `WriteAheadLog` per orphan, resolves the target server, and drains — plus a policy for WALs whose run was never created server-side (see G-1) and for cleanup of `.artifact.N.bin` spill files.

claim: §6.1 asserts "the existing lock/advertisement machinery is the substrate — `repo.lock` + `servers.json` already let a second process discover the live server and upgrade to HTTP … the first process becomes the server, later processes connect to it." No SDK process ever becomes a lock holder today, and `servers.json` plays no part in the upgrade path, so the load-bearing half of the ruling's mechanism does not exist.
evidence: `acquire_lock` is called from exactly two places, both in the CLI: `cairn server` (cairn/cli.py:224) and `cairn ui` (cli.py:375). `LocalTransport` only *reads* the lock and never acquires it (cairn/sdk/local.py:62-73), and it raises `_RepoServedByOtherError` only when `holder.get("mode") == "server"` — a `cairn ui` holder (mode `"ui"`) is silently ignored. `add_live_server` is called once, by `cairn ui` (cli.py:399); `cairn server` never advertises. `servers.json` is read only by `read_live_servers` for notebook card rendering (cairn/sdk/elements.py:185, datadir.py:234-259) — never by `Run`'s transport resolution. `acquire_lock` is strictly exclusive against any live pid (datadir.py:153-158), so two concurrent training processes racing to spawn need arbitration that does not exist.
suggestion: Spell out the new mechanics: which lock mode an SDK-spawned server takes, how the spawn race is arbitrated (create-exclusive lock then bind, retry-and-connect on EEXIST), who advertises to `servers.json`, and — critically — what a client does when the spawning process exits while it is still writing (server re-election / re-resolution loop). "Lifetime = the spawning process" plus "the client WAL covers crashes" does not cover a *peer* process whose server URL just died.

claim: §7's "re-minted transparently by the UI's `artifactUrl` funnel near expiry" is not implementable through today's funnel: `artifactUrl` is a synchronous pure function and one of its consumers is a cairn-plot API that is typed synchronous. Minting requires a server round-trip, i.e. async.
evidence: `artifactUrl: (hash: string) => \`/api/artifacts/${hash}\`` (cairn/cairn/ui/src/api/client.ts:117). It is consumed inline in JSX/`fetch` at 51 sites across 20 files, and is passed as the callback to cairn-plot's `createEndpointDataSource(artifactUrl: (hash: string) => string): DataSource` (vendor/cairn-plot/ui/src/lib/cairn-plot/viewport/data-sources.ts:99) from four card components (viewport-registry.tsx:61, MeshVisualCard.tsx:61, VolumeVisualCard.tsx:58, PointCloudVisualCard.tsx:78). Only 10 of the 51 uses are actually `src=`/`href=` browser tags; the rest are programmatic `fetch()`/`downloadArtifact()` calls, contradicting §3's "single formatter feeding ~30 `/
suggestion: Specify the minting model concretely: either (a) hand the browser a single long-lived per-session signing capability so `artifactUrl` stays sync and pure, or (b) declare that a batch/prefetch mint runs on connect and refresh, with `artifactUrl` reading a cached, non-expired signature; and state that the cairn-plot `DataSource` seam must accept an async URL resolver (a change to the companion Host API spec).

section: §7 (signed artifact URLs) × §9 (references resolve to a simple URL)
claim: The two rulings collide unhandled: a live reference URL is `/api/query?...`, which 302-redirects to a *bare, unsigned* `/api/artifacts/{digest}`. Under §7's regime that redirect target is auth-gated, so every ``/`
evidence: `RedirectResponse(url=f"/api/artifacts/{art.digest}", status_code=302, ...)` — no signature, no query string carried over (cairn/server/routes/query.py:60-62). `artifacts.router` is registered with `dependencies=[Depends(require("read"))]` (cairn/server/app.py:186-200), so an unauthenticated browser-tag fetch of the redirect target 401s. §9 explicitly says a reference "rides the descriptor as a plain https `src` ref" and §7 says browser tags cannot carry headers.
suggestion: Extend the signing rule to `/api/query` itself: accept `sig`/`exp` on the query endpoint and propagate a freshly-minted signature onto the 302 `Location`. Then say what `exp` on the redirect means relative to `exp` on the incoming query URL, and how a report authored months earlier obtains a signature at view time.

claim: §4's lint-enforced "No `track ↔ server` imports in either direction" is incompatible with §6.1's stated trigger mechanism, and cairn-core as scoped in §4 has no home for the pieces §6.1 needs.
evidence: The lock/advertisement layer lives in the server package: `from ..server.storage.datadir import DataDir, RepoLockedError` (cairn/sdk/run.py:41) and `from ..server.storage.datadir import read_live_servers` (cairn/sdk/elements.py:185). §6.1 keeps both as the resolver's trigger. §4 defines cairn-core as "query grammar (`_OPERATORS`, QuerySpec, URL encode/decode), wire models, WAL op vocabulary, API version" — the datadir/lock/`servers.json` layer is not in that list, and it is inherently filesystem-and-process machinery, not a wire contract.
suggestion: Either add a `discovery`/`datadir` module to cairn-core's charter (and say so), or state that cairn-track's local-target resolution reads `repo.lock`/`servers.json` as a *file format* it owns, with the format specified in cairn-core rather than importing server code.

claim: §7 and the S3 migration step specify token auth for "the plugin WebSocket", and §8 counts "the WS constructor" among the ~5 endpoint-config sites — but §11.4 rules the plugin system dropped, and the plugin WS is the only WebSocket that exists.
evidence: The tree's only websocket route is `@router.websocket("/ws/plugin/{run_id}/{metric_name:path}")` (cairn/server/routes/plugin_ws.py:356), and the only client constructor is `new WebSocket(\`${protocol}//${window.location.host}/ws/plugin/...\`)` in PluginCard.tsx:269. App wiring notes it "gates itself (session cookie only, checked before accept())" (cairn/server/app.py:206-210). Dropping plugins also removes the Pyodide/Plotly CDN deps §8 asks to inventory (PluginCard.tsx:62,132-133).
suggestion: Delete the WS-token-auth item from §7 and S3, drop "the WS constructor" from §8's site count (making it ~4), and move Pyodide/Plotly out of §8's CDN inventory — or, if a WS is expected to survive for live-run streaming, name that new endpoint instead of the plugin one.

claim: The enumeration of the five drift bugs is wrong on one item and the claim that a client-vs-live-server conformance suite "would have caught all five" is false for two of them.
evidence: Client `list_artifact_versions` GETs `/api/artifact-families/{family_id}/versions` (cairn/sdk/reader.py:1179) and the server serves exactly that route (`@router.get("/artifact-families/{family_id}/versions")` under `prefix="/api"`, cairn/server/routes/artifact_registry.py:15,138) — "versions" is NOT drifted. The three real HTTP mismatches are resolve (client GET `/api/projects/{p}/artifact-families/resolve`, reader.py:1182, vs server POST `/api/projects/{p}/resolve-artifact-ref`, artifact_registry.py:226), inputs (`/input-artifacts` reader.py:1185 vs `/runs/{id}/inputs` artifact_registry.py:255) and outputs (`/output-artifacts` reader.py:1188 vs `/runs/{id}/outputs` artifact_registry.py:261). The other two are in-process `AttributeError`s, not wire drift: `artifact_registry_ops.resolve_artifact` (reader.py:1004) and `.get_lineage` (reader.py:1018) do not exist — the real names are `resolve_ref` (artifact_registry_ops.py:367) and `get_lineage_graph` (artifact_registry_ops.py:460).
suggestion: Correct the enumeration to resolve/inputs/outputs + two `_LocalBackend` op-name errors, and drop the claim that the conformance suite covers the latter two (it does not — they are Python-attribute drift, killed only by S2's deletion of `_LocalBackend`). Add a note that S0's "fix the five" must also fix the ~6th, see G-17.

claim: "No drift by construction" holds only for the operator *table*; the encoder is lossy for list-valued operators and the two sides coerce values differently, so filters silently round-trip to non-matches today. §5's encoder/decoder is scoped to URL shape and never mentions value serialization.
evidence: `_build_params` stringifies every filter value with `str(value)` (cairn/sdk/query_urls.py:62), and `RunQuery.latest_url` feeds its filters straight into it (reader.py:733-744). So `filter(status__in=["completed","killed"])` emits `status__in=%5B%27completed%27%2C+%27killed%27%5D`, while the server splits `in` values on commas: `coerced = [_coerce(v) for v in value.split(",")]` (cairn/server/query_resolver.py:165-166), yielding `["['completed'", " 'killed']"]` — zero matches, no error. Separately the client compares native Python values (`_OPERATORS[op](actual, value)`, reader.py:691) while the server compares against `_coerce`d strings (query_resolver.py:240-253, 330).
suggestion: Make cairn-core's grammar own value encoding as explicitly as it owns operators: a typed encode/decode pair per operator (list operators comma-joined with escaping, bools/None canonicalized), plus a round-trip property test in the conformance suite (`encode(decode(u)) == u`, `decode(encode(spec)) == spec`).

claim: Retiring `_LocalBackend` also deletes the zip-archive read path, which §6.1's ephemeral server does not cover (it spawns against a `.cairn` data dir, not an archive). A shipped feature disappears with no migration named.
evidence: `Reader(repo=<something>.zip)` unpacks to a tempdir and constructs `_LocalBackend(repo_path)` (cairn/sdk/reader.py:1393-1397, `_load_zip_to_tempdir`); export/import of those archives is a server feature (cairn/server/routes/import_export.py, registered under the write-role loop in app.py:204-205). §6.1 only describes spawning "for the (defaulted) `.cairn` data dir".
suggestion: Say explicitly whether `Reader("run.zip")` survives — e.g. the `[local]` extra unpacks the zip into a temp data dir and spawns the ephemeral server against it — or declare the zip-read path removed and point users at `cairn-server --data <unpacked>`.

claim: "auth disabled on loopback (same-user semantics, as the direct-DB mode had)" is factually wrong about the security model: loopback TCP carries no user identity, so this is a privilege *widening* relative to direct-DB, not a preservation of it.
evidence: Direct-DB access was gated by filesystem permissions on the `.cairn` tree (`DataDir.__init__` mkdirs, cairn/server/storage/datadir.py:52-60; lock file created 0o644 at datadir.py:139). The proposed replacement is `create_app(..., auth_enabled=False)` bound to `127.0.0.1:<ephemeral>` — and with `auth_enabled=False` CORS also opens to `allow_origins=["*"]` (cairn/server/app.py:159). On a shared machine (a cluster login node is the exact target workload) any other local user can connect to that port and get unauthenticated read+write to another user's runs, and any web page the user visits can XHR the port.
suggestion: Require the ephemeral server to mint a random per-process token, write it into the `repo.lock`/`servers.json` entry (readable only via the already-permission-checked data dir), and have connecting clients present it — keeping `auth_enabled=True`. Or bind to a Unix domain socket instead of loopback TCP.

section: §6 ("Kept and promoted: the existing HTTP client WAL becomes THE durability story")
claim: The WAL being promoted to the durability story is not concurrency-safe, and its checkpoint scheme can silently mark unsent entries as sent. The spec adopts it as "existing" machinery without listing these as work.
evidence: `WriteAheadLog.append` mutates `self._seq` and writes to a shared handle with no lock (cairn/sdk/wal.py:79-87), while metric batches are flushed from a daemon thread (`threading.Thread(target=self._run, name="cairn-metric-flush", daemon=True)`, cairn/sdk/buffer.py:35-36) concurrently with main-thread artifact/param/log appends (transport.py:169,178,230). `checkpoint(seq)` overwrites a bare scalar (wal.py:118-120) and each op checkpoints its own seq on success (transport.py:158-159,172-173,181-182,245-246), so if seq 6 completes before seq 5 fails, the checkpoint reads 6 and `pending()` (`if seq <= cp: continue`, wal.py:135-137) drops seq 5 forever. `append_artifact` also names its spill file from `self._seq + 1` before the increment (wal.py:102) — two concurrent large artifacts collide on one filename.
suggestion: Add to §6/S2: a lock around append+fsync, a monotonic `checkpoint = max(existing, seq)` plus a per-entry acked set (or in-flight-window tracking) so out-of-order acks cannot skip, and allocate the spill filename from the same locked sequence bump.

section: §6 ("every op is seq-numbered into the WAL before/with send")
claim: Several ops are not WAL'd today, so "every op" describes a target state, not existing machinery — and the gap has a user-visible consequence for the replay story the spec promises.
evidence: `create_run` (transport.py:150-151), `finish_run` (transport.py:189-193), `set_tags` (transport.py:195-196) and `set_notes` (transport.py:198+) post directly with no `self._wal.append(...)`. The replay handler has a `"finish"` branch (transport.py:347-351) that is dead code — nothing ever appends a `finish` op (only occurrence of the string is that branch). Consequence: a process that dies with pending WAL and is later drained gets its metrics/logs/artifacts but is never finished; it stays `running` until `_reap_stale_runs` marks it stale, and that reaper is request-driven off `GET /api/runs` (cairn/server/routes/runs.py:19,22,68), not a background loop.
suggestion: List the missing WAL ops (create/finish/tags/notes) as S2 work, and state whether a replayed `finish` should overwrite a reaper-assigned status.

claim: This is described as a URL-shape change for "the python emitters", but the embed path is a cross-origin, authenticated, server-stateful flow once the UI moves off the server's origin — and the plot entry does not implement the `?sid=` mode at all.
evidence: `CardElement.iframe_html` builds `src = f"{server.rstrip('/')}/embed/card?sid={sid}"` after POSTing the spec to the server (cairn/sdk/elements.py:88-91,232-248) with `sandbox="allow-scripts allow-same-origin"`. The embed bundle then fetches the spec with a hardcoded *relative* path: `fetch(\`/api/embed/specs/${sid}\`)` (cairn/cairn/ui/src/embed-main.tsx:178). The spec store is per-app and in-memory (`app.state.embed_specs = EmbedSpecStore()`, cairn/server/app.py:146-149). The plot entry explicitly refuses the sid mode: `throw new Error("?sid= descriptor loading is not available yet (Phase C).")` (vendor/cairn-plot/ui/src/plot-bootstrap.tsx:139). Note both `embed.html` and `plot.html` already exist as vite entries (cairn/cairn/ui/vite.config.ts:41-45) and are served from bytes read at startup (app.py:250-279), so §3's "`/embed/card` + `/plot` are server routes" understates what is already static.
suggestion: Specify the new embed URL shape end-to-end: `<ui-origin>/embed.html?endpoint=<server>&sid=<id>[&token=…]`, the endpoint-aware fetch inside `embed-main.tsx`, CORS + auth on `/api/embed/specs/{sid}`, and the sandbox/token posture for a cross-origin iframe. Say whether the notebook `CardElement` fallback (no server) still applies when the UI origin and server origin differ.

claim: §9 presents `/api/compare` as an existing URL-addressable reference target; it is POST-only and therefore not a URL reference at all — and §11.5 of the same document defers GET-ifying it "indefinitely". The two sections contradict each other.
evidence: `@router.post("/compare")` (cairn/server/routes/compare.py:21-22) — the only compare route. §11.5: "a future multi-run series url (GET-ified /api/compare feeding one chart) would cost cairn-plot nothing … deferrable indefinitely." `/api/runs/select` does not exist yet either (it is proposed in §5).
suggestion: Remove `/api/compare` from §9's list of reference URLs and reference §11.5's deferral there, or promote GET `/api/compare` into S1 with an explicit selector-to-query-params encoding.

section: §5 ("the server twin `resolve_run_ids` already exists"; "the card-spec `QueryRunSelector` dialect is re-expressed over it")
claim: `resolve_run_ids` exists but implements the *weak fourth dialect*, not the `_OPERATORS` predicate grammar §5 wants `/api/runs/select` to accept, and it is unrouted dead code. Separately, the weak dialect has three implementations, not one, so "re-expressed" is a three-site change.
evidence: `resolve_run_ids(db, selector: QueryRunSelectorSpec, *, project)` takes only `mode: latest-n|newest-per-name`, `name_pattern` glob, all-of `tags`, `n` (cairn/server/query_resolver.py:455-509) — no predicates, no operators. Grepping the tree, `resolve_run_ids` has zero callers and no route registers it (cairn/server/routes/query.py imports only `parse_query_params`/`resolve`). The dialect's three implementations: `class QueryRunSelector` (cairn/sdk/card_spec.py:169-177), `interface QueryRunSelector` + `resolveRunSelectorFromRuns` (cairn/cairn/ui/src/lib/run-selector.ts:31-56,104-131), and the server port `_matches_name`/`_matches_tags`/`resolve_run_ids` (query_resolver.py:246-282,470). §3's "the grammar exists, in three mirrored places" also omits `run-selector.ts`, which query_resolver.py:249 documents itself as a "faithful port" of.
suggestion: Correct §5 to say `resolve_run_ids` gives the selector *plumbing* but must be re-based onto the predicate grammar, and name all three sites of the weak dialect (plus the server's `_matches_name` glob semantics) as the re-expression surface.

section: §6.1 ("install cairn-track[local] or point CAIRN_SERVER at one") + §11.6 (connect screen / `cairn ui --server`)
claim: The spec's user-facing error message names an environment variable that does not exist, and the config-file key the CLI persists for a server URL is never read — a sixth shipping client/config drift of the same class §3 enumerates, which the connect-screen/persistence design in §11.6 will inherit.
evidence: The only repo/server env var is `CAIRN_REPO` (cairn/config.py:189, 142, 147; `cairn://host:port` is parsed at config.py:129-131). There is no `CAIRN_SERVER` anywhere in the tree. Separately, `cairn configure --server` writes `existing["server"] = server` (cairn/cli.py:715) and `cairn login --ssh` writes `existing["server"] = server_url` (cli.py:907), but `resolve_target`/`resolve_server` only ever read `cfg["repo"]` (config.py:149, 194) — so the persisted server URL has no effect on any subsequent command.
suggestion: Fix the error text to `CAIRN_REPO=cairn://host:port`, and add the `server`-vs-`repo` config-key mismatch to S0's drift-bug list. Then state which key §11.6's connect screen / `cairn ui --server` persistence writes and reads.

section: §9 ("the RefStore's `contentKey` is the resolved DIGEST (302 target / envelope field) — free content identity")
claim: For the browser-tag consumption path §9 itself blesses, the digest is not observable at all; for the programmatic path it is observable only under CORS conditions the spec does not require.
evidence: An `` gives JavaScript no access to the redirect chain — there is no API to read the 302 `Location` or the final URL of an image load. For `fetch`, `response.url` after a cross-origin redirect requires the redirect *target* to also pass CORS; §7 only adds `--allow-origin` in auth-on mode and the artifacts route currently exposes only `Content-Range`/`Content-Length`/`Accept-Ranges` (cairn/server/app.py:163). The `format=json` envelope returns a relative `"url": f"/api/artifacts/{art.digest}"` (cairn/server/routes/query.py:47-56), so obtaining the digest costs an extra authenticated round trip the tag path cannot make.
suggestion: Either require `/api/query` to echo the digest in a CORS-exposed response header (e.g. `X-Cairn-Digest`, added to `expose_headers`) so a HEAD/GET can key the RefStore, or state that live URL references key the RefStore by the *reference URL* and only acquire a digest identity after an explicit `.pin()`/envelope fetch.

claim: Moving predicates server-side relocates the cap rather than removing it: `/api/runs` enforces a hard `limit ≤ 1000` at the route, and the spec specifies no pagination for selector results.
evidence: `limit: int = Query(default=50, ge=1, le=1000)` (cairn/server/routes/runs.py:61). Client-side, `RunQuery.list()` passes `limit=self._limit_n or 1000` (cairn/sdk/reader.py:682), so `.limit(5000)` already 422s today. Note also that `.limit(n)` is applied to the *fetch* before filtering (reader.py:682) and again after (reader.py:702-703), so `.limit(5).filter(...)` today filters within only 5 fetched rows — a second silent-truncation mode the spec does not mention.
suggestion: State the pagination contract for `/api/runs` and `/api/runs/select` under the predicate grammar (cursor or offset, and whether `limit` is pre- or post-predicate), and note the `.limit()`-before-filter semantics change users will observe.

section: §4 ("Depends on cairn-core + httpx ONLY") × §9 ("cairn-plot depends on neither cairn-track nor the grammar, ever")
claim: The dependency graph omits the edge that exists today: cairn-track hard-depends on cairn-plot and registers types into it. §9 only rules out the reverse edge, leaving the existing forward edge and its registration seam unaddressed.
evidence: `dependencies = ["cairn-plot", "fastapi…", …]` in pyproject.toml:20-21 for `name = "cairn-track"` (pyproject.toml:2). `cairn/plot.py` re-exports the whole `cairn_plot` surface and wires `register_data_ref_type(DataRef)` (plot.py:34,47) plus `register_resolvers(...)` for table/pointcloud/mesh handlers (plot.py:34,58-90). So cairn-plot already has a pluggable notion of a cairn `DataRef` — which sits uneasily with §9's "no `cp.Repo`, no query assembly, no grammar, no pin logic in cairn-plot". §4's "cairn-core + httpx ONLY" is also contradicted by pillow/numpy/zstandard/click/platformdirs/psutil/pynvml (pyproject.toml:20-36).
suggestion: Draw the `track → plot` edge in §4's diagram and say what happens to `cairn/plot.py`'s registration shim under the split — specifically whether `register_data_ref_type` survives (a `DataRef` that stringifies to a URL would make it unnecessary) — and soften "cairn-core + httpx ONLY" to "no server-side deps (no FastAPI, no uvicorn, no sqlite)".

claim: Two ruled-in decisions have no step in the migration plan: the ephemeral local server (§6.1) and dropping the plugin system (§11.4). S2 removes the direct-DB paths those rulings replace, so the plan as written ships a regression at S2.
evidence: S2 reads "retire `LocalTransport`/`local_wal`/direct-DB reads" with no counterpart step for spawning a loopback server; §6.1's `[local]` extra is only mentioned in §6.1 and §11.1. S3 lists "WS token auth" for a subsystem §11.4 drops (see G-7). Nothing in S0–S6 removes `cairn/sdk/plugins.py`, `cairn/server/routes/plugin_ws.py`, `plugin_webrtc.py`, or `PluginCard.tsx`.
suggestion: Add the ephemeral-server work into S2 (before or alongside the direct-DB retirement, so no release is left without a zero-setup path) and a plugin-removal step (S0 or S2), and delete "WS token auth" from S3.

section: §8 ("Degraded-offline behavior is already good … keep it") + CDN inventory
claim: The offline claim is contradicted by a hard CDN stylesheet dependency in all three HTML entries, which §8 lists as merely "inventoried" — with plugins dropped (§11.4), FontAwesome is the *only* remaining CDN dep and it affects every page, not an optional feature.
evidence: `<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/font-awesome/6.5.2/css/all.min.css" …>` appears at line 12 of cairn/cairn/ui/index.html, embed.html and plot.html. Pyodide/Plotly are confined to PluginCard.tsx:62,132-133, which §11.4 removes.
suggestion: Make vendoring FontAwesome (or swapping to a bundled icon set) an explicit S4 task rather than an "inventory" item, since "documented as an online-only feature" is not an option for the app chrome.

claim: Two unstated consequences: no persistent server signing secret exists today, and hourly re-minting fights the immutable cache headers the artifact route deliberately sets — re-downloading large media on every expiry window.
evidence: `cairn/server/auth.py` stores only *hashed* secrets (`hash_secret`, auth.py:76-78; tokens at 109-115, sessions at 195, OTPs at 254-257) and generates per-item random secrets (`generate_secret`, auth.py:81-82); there is no long-lived server key anywhere, so a restart would invalidate every outstanding signed URL. Meanwhile `/api/artifacts/{digest}` sets `_IMMUTABLE = "public, max-age=31536000, immutable"` (cairn/server/routes/artifacts.py:20-21,109) — a cache keyed on the full URL, so changing `sig`/`exp` produces a cache miss on content that never changed. "Revoking the token invalidates its urls" additionally requires a token-validity DB read on every artifact request, and cannot evict copies already in the browser cache.
suggestion: Specify where the signing secret is persisted (data dir, 0600, generated on first start) and its rotation semantics; and decouple the cache key from the signature — e.g. sign a scope (`token_id` + digest-prefix or run) carried in a cookie/header-free `sig` that stays stable for its whole validity window, or move `sig`/`exp` out of the cache key via a `Vary`-able mechanism.

section: §7 ("SSH-key auth promoted to the primary path (exists today)")
claim: Promoting SSH-key auth to the primary path makes an external binary on the *server* a hard requirement of the primary login flow — currently an acceptable limitation for an opt-in path.
evidence: `ssh_verify` shells out to `ssh-keygen -Y verify` and returns HTTP 501 when the binary is absent: `if ssh_keygen is None: raise HTTPException(status_code=501, detail="ssh-keygen not available on server")` (cairn/server/routes/auth.py:131-138,166). Slim server containers routinely omit openssh-client. Keys are matched against an operator-managed `DATA_DIR/auth/authorized_keys` with a `role=<admin|write|read>` comment (cairn/server/auth.py:335,357-363).
suggestion: Note the `ssh-keygen`-on-server requirement (and the operator-managed `authorized_keys` provisioning step) in §7, and state the fallback when it is missing — Bearer tokens should remain a first-class, documented path rather than a CI/bot-only one.
